2970: Signs of risk are indicators of significant psychological distress and greater emotional vulnerability. They may arise from changes in the person’s behaviour, emotions or ability to function.
2972: Marked changes in behaviour (isolation, agitation, apathy)
2973: Expressions of hopelessness, emptiness or a lack of meaning
2974: A marked decline in personal, social or professional functioning
2975: Increased use of alcohol or other substances
2976: Difficulty coping with emotions or everyday situations
2977: Very intense emotional reactions, or reactions out of proportion to the situation
2979: Functional incapacity refers to the person’s difficulty or inability to carry out everyday tasks and maintain their usual functioning.
2981: Difficulty carrying out basic tasks (self-care, work, study or daily responsibilities)
2982: Inability to make simple decisions or solve everyday problems
2983: Frequent absences or a significant drop in performance
2984: A feeling of being “stuck”, unable to move forward or act
2985: Difficulty maintaining social relationships or usual responsibilities
2987: Persistent symptoms are emotional, cognitive or physical reactions that continue over time without significant improvement, interfering with the person’s wellbeing.
2992: Constant emotional tiredness or a feeling of exhaustion
2993: Difficulty concentrating or a feeling of mental overload
2994: Physical symptoms associated with stress (tension, pain, fatigue)
2996: It is not to replace initial support, but to ensure that the person receives the type of help best suited to their needs.
